The libFuzzer entry point is only the unscored container boundary. This statement is the first project parser read that creates vulnerability-relevant frame-geometry state.

The staged patch adds an explicit `else if (cdef_info->allocated_mi_rows != num_mi_rows)` branch that frees and rebuilds `cdef_sync->cdef_row_mt`. In the vulnerable source, AddressSanitizer proves only that the crashing object was allocated at `alloccommon.c:199`; the smaller-earlier-allocation conclusion comes from source semantics, because both same-frame allocation here and later scheduling in `cdef_sb_row_worker_hook()` derive their row bounds from the current `cm->mi_params.mi_rows` with the same ceil(rows/64x64) formula. A row-sync array rebuilt for the later frame would therefore match the later schedule, so the saved overread requires a smaller earlier allocation to have remained live.
